title: A Behavioural Intervention Study To Increase Flavonoid Consumption
official: A Randomised, Single-Blinded Behavioural Intervention Study Aimed at Increasing Flavonoid Consumption in Young Adults
summary: The present study aims to assess whether a behavioural intervention can lead to increased and sustained flavonoid consumption. The investigators will specifically test whether knowledge of the benefits of flavonoid intake for protection against mental stress (Stress condition) or knowledge of the acute benefits of flavonoid intake (Acute condition) will result in higher intake of flavonoids compared to knowledge of the long-term impact of flavonoid intake for cardiovascular and brain health (Control). The investigators will further assess whether changes in flavonoid intake is accompanied by changes in other aspects of the diet (macro and micronutrients) as well as improvements in vascular and brain physiology. The first research hypothesis is that participants who receive specific nutritional information about the immediate (acute) effects of flavonoid intake will increase their flavonoid intake at 1 week and 4 weeks in comparison to those who receive general information about the benefits of flavonoid intake for health (control group). Likewise, participants who receive stress-specific flavonoid information will increase their flavonoid intake at 1 week and 4 weeks overall, and around stressful periods, compared to those who receive general information about the benefits of flavonoid intake for health (control group). A third hypothesis is that participants with higher daily flavonoid intake after 4 weeks will show greater endothelial function and lower declines in endothelial dysfunction in the context of stress (increased resilience to stress).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male or Female
* Aged 18 to 45 years old
* Have a smartphone
* Do not smoke
* Do not have a history of cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, inflammatory or neurological diseases.
* Do not suffer from hypertension, diabetes, asthma, high cholesterol, immune condition and anaemia.
* Currently not taking any long-term medication
* Do not consume more than 14 units of alcohol per week
* Not on any weight-restricted diets (e.g. weight loss jabs)
* You do not have a history of/ diagnosis of disordered eating Females with a regular menstruating cycle or were taking an oral contraceptive pill that included inactive/ placebo days.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Do not have a smartphone
* Smoke
* Have a history of cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, inflammatory or neurological diseases.
* Suffer from hypertension, diabetes, asthma, high cholesterol, immune condition and anaemia.
* Currently taking any long-term medication
* Consume more than 14 units of alcohol per week
* On weight-restricted diets (e.g. weight loss jabs)
* Have a history of/ diagnosis of disordered eating Females who do not have a regular menstruating cycle or are not taking an oral contraceptive pill that included inactive/ placebo days.
